promise.text: Three questions show whether a ceramic piece was made to last.

meta.hypothesis: Quiet serif covers earn saves in craft audiences.

caption:
Good glaze is easy to photograph and hard to fake.

Before you buy a handmade cup, turn it over. These three questions take a minute and tell you more than the listing does.

#Ceramics #Handmade

slides.headline: Turn the cup over first.
slides.alt: Burgundy cover with the serif headline Turn the cup over first above three overlapping cards.
slides.visual_prompt: Three overlapping cards in sand and cream. Composed by the engine.

slides.headline: The foot of a cup tells you how carefully the rest was made.
slides.alt: Cream slide with a quote saying the foot of a cup shows how carefully the rest was made.
slides.visual_prompt: Serif pull quote with a thin vertical sand rule.

slides.headline: Ask these before buying.
slides.alt: Three questions to ask: is the foot smooth, does the glaze pool evenly, does it sit flat.

slides.headline: Heavy is not sturdy.
slides.myth: A thick wall means a strong cup
slides.fact: Even walls matter more than thick ones
slides.alt: Dark slide correcting the myth that thick walls mean strength: even walls matter more.
slides.visual_prompt: Struck-through myth above a sand fact panel.

slides.headline: Buy the cup you can flip.
slides.body: If a listing hides the foot, ask for one more photo.
slides.cta: Save this for your next market
slides.alt: Burgundy closing slide asking the reader to request a photo of the foot and save the post.
slides.visual_prompt: Calm burgundy close with one sand action panel.
